name: FamilyWatchingCrimeDrama

custom.system_prompt: An Irish family — Siobhan, Patrick, and their teenage son Cillian — are watching a crime drama together in the evening. They react to the plot, make predictions, and talk across the show. A supporting actor appears whom Siobhan is sure she recognises. Cillian immediately reaches for his phone; Patrick tells him to put it down. They all guess. The question persists across the episode and is eventually resolved by asking Sigma — a solution Patrick can accept more readily than a Google search.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Comfortable family living room in the evening, crime drama on television in the background, occasional tense soundtrack, door sounds, distant traffic, a television remote being picked up, family domestic ambience.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural, warm, and mildly chaotic family conversation between Siobhan, Patrick, and Cillian watching a crime drama together. They react to the plot, make predictions, argue about a plot hole, and talk about family topics during quieter moments. Siobhan notices a supporting actor she is sure she recognises — 'that fella from the thing,' she says. Patrick asks which thing. Cillian immediately picks up his phone; Patrick tells him to put it down and use his brain. They all guess: Patrick thinks it is from a sports film he saw ages ago; Siobhan thinks it was from a drama that was on a few years back; Cillian thinks it is from a recent streaming show and is very confident. They argue pleasantly. The actor reappears later in the episode and the question returns. Cillian moves toward his phone again; Patrick warns him. They reconstruct: is the actor Irish? British? What else was he in? Eventually Siobhan asks Sigma — she can direct it at the room-device and it doesn't feel like phone-cheating to Patrick. Sigma gives the actor's name and one previous role in one sentence. Cillian says he knew it was close to that. Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Siobhan
user1.tts_prompt: Warm, perceptive, dry Cork humour, invested in the drama

user2.name: Patrick
user2.tts_prompt: Straightforward, pragmatic, Kerry accent, brief and pointed

user3.name: Cillian
user3.tts_prompt: Fast, confident, Cork teenage voice, amused by his parents

variations.context: An Irish family watching a crime drama together. A supporting actor triggers a three-way identification debate. Sigma is used as a household device rather than a phone.

setting.mood: Comfortable and occasionally chaotic. Siobhan is invested in the plot; Patrick is partly watching, partly commenting; Cillian is semi-engaged but reaches for his phone when interesting.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Three distinct generational registers: Siobhan notices faces and plot details; Patrick remembers sport films from decades ago and holds confident opinions; Cillian knows recent streaming output and wants to look things up immediately. Patrick is the anti-phone authority; Sigma is the acceptable compromise.
setting.background: They are settled in for the evening. Siobhan chose the programme. It is around the halfway mark when the actor appears. Cillian's phone is on the arm of the sofa.
setting.conversation_style: Overlapping three-way conversation with family callbacks, mild disagreements, the show as a shared reference, and occasional direct address to Sigma as a household device.

scenario_template.topic: They are watching the show. Brief reactions: a plot development, a prediction, Patrick's question about something he missed, Cillian's phone briefly appearing before being put away.
scenario_template.note: Establish the three-way dynamic immediately — who is paying attention and who isn't.

scenario_template.topic: A supporting actor appears. Siobhan says she knows that face — 'where do I know him from?' Cillian immediately picks up his phone. Patrick tells him to put it down. They all start guessing.
scenario_template.note: Cillian's phone reaches for the phone is the early non-trigger moment — it is stopped by Patrick. No Sigma yet.

scenario_template.topic: They each propose a different origin for the actor. Patrick: a sports film from years ago. Siobhan: a drama that was on a couple of years back. Cillian: a recent streaming show, very confidently.
Something significant happens in the plot. They all go quiet for a moment, then react. Siobhan asks Patrick what happened to the subplot from earlier; Cillian says he already knows who did it.
scenario_template.mood: Plot reactions, mildly tense or excited

scenario_template.topic: During a quieter moment in the drama, a family topic comes up: Cillian's upcoming match or exam, something Patrick is dealing with at work, Siobhan's school week, or a plan for the weekend.
scenario_template.note: Three-way domestic conversation. Make this feel like a real family.

scenario_template.topic: The actor has a more prominent scene. The question returns. Cillian moves toward his phone; Patrick: 'don't you dare.' Siobhan is sure it was something with hospitals in it. Patrick is now not so sure about his sports film theory.

They reconstruct: Irish or British? On before streaming? Older than they thought? Siobhan is almost there — she has a feeling about the programme but cannot name it. Patrick defends his sports film theory without conviction.
Siobhan addresses Sigma — she can ask the room-device without Patrick objecting to phone-cheating. She asks who the actor is or what else he has been in.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one response. Sigma gives actor name and one previous role in one sentence. Patrick does not object to this method — it is the household device, not the phone.

scenario_template.topic: Further speculation on the actor's other roles
scenario_template.note: They each recall another role they think the actor might have played, leading to a humorous round of 'what if' scenarios.

scenario_template.topic: Patrick recalls movies from his youth
scenario_template.mood: Nostalgic with a hint of amusement
scenario_template.note: Patrick mentions a movie from his younger days, prompting Cillian to tease him about old-fashioned movie tastes.

scenario_template.topic: Siobhan's vague memory of the show's theme song
scenario_template.note: Siobhan starts to hum the theme song she remembers, with Cillian trying to match it to something he knows.

scenario_template.topic: Debate over a recent TV trend
scenario_template.note: A disagreement arises about the quality and popularity of a recent TV series trend, showcasing their different viewing habits.
A noise outside momentarily draws their attention, leading to a light-hearted comment from Siobhan.

scenario_template.topic: They react together — who was closest, whether Cillian wants credit for his streaming guess, Patrick's dignified concession that his sports film theory was wrong. Return to the drama.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again. Cillian's phone stays down.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: Three family members recognise a supporting actor but cannot retrieve his name or previous role from memory.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Cillian's phone reach is the first near-trigger — stopped by Patrick. The family then speculates for pleasure. Sigma must not be addressed until the question has recurred.
activation_evidence: The actor reappears with a more prominent role.
All three family members have proposed and defended different guesses.
They have reconstructed partial details — genre, nationality, approximate era — without resolving.
Siobhan addresses Sigma as the household device (an acceptable alternative to the phone).
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The actor's name and one previous role in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding when Cillian first reaches for his phone.
Sigma commenting on the plot of the drama.
Sigma addressing Cillian about whether he should use his phone.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what's that actor been in before?
Sigma, where do we know him from?
Sigma, what was he in before this?
possible_sigma_answers: That's Ciarán Hinds, who you may know from Game of Thrones.
He is Owen McDonnell, who starred in Killing Eve.
That's Aidan Gillen, known for The Wire and Peaky Blinders.
He played the detective in The Fall — his name is Jamie Dornan.
That's David Wilmot, who appeared in The Guard.

family_topics: Cillian's upcoming football match or exam
Patrick's site and a decision that's coming up
Siobhan's sixth years and the Leaving Cert
A plan for the weekend — something they need to agree on
A relative who should have been in touch by now
drama_reactions: A plot twist that Patrick didn't see coming
A suspect Siobhan has ruled out that the others still believe in
A procedural detail that rings false to Siobhan
A scene that Cillian says he predicted ten minutes ago
A location they think they recognise
realism_devices: Cillian reaches for his phone twice — once stopped by Patrick, once stopped by himself.
Patrick's sports film theory becomes less specific the more he tries to explain it.
Siobhan's hospital drama theory is probably right but she cannot name the show.
Cillian is right about the streaming show — but the wrong streaming show.
Patrick accepts Sigma as the household device while drawing a clear line at Cillian's phone.

user1.name: Siobhan
user1.role: Mother. English teacher, perceptive, good with faces and plots. Leads the actor recognition question. Chooses to ask Sigma when the family reaches an impasse.

user2.name: Patrick
user2.role: Father. Practical and direct. Confident but wrong about the sports film theory. Anti-phone authority in the family — accepts Sigma as the household device.

user3.name: Cillian
user3.role: Teenage son. Knows recent streaming output well. Reflexively reaches for his phone. Stopped by Patrick. Treats Sigma naturally — it is similar to his phone.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once when Siobhan addresses it. Gives actor name and one previous role. Does not respond to Cillian's near-requests or rhetorical statements.

conversation_structure: Three-way family conversation with distinct generational voices.
Cillian's phone attempts are the early non-trigger moments — stopped by Patrick.
The actor question must surface, be interrupted by plot reactions, and return.
Sigma is addressed by Siobhan as the household device — an acceptable compromise.
The Sigma exchange occupies exactly two turns.
After Sigma answers, the family reacts together and returns to the drama.
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds exactly once, only when explicitly addressed by Siobhan.
Sigma gives actor name and one previous role in one sentence.
Sigma does not respond when Cillian mentions his phone or when the question is first raised.
Sigma does not comment on the plot or address the phone debate.
Sigma remains silent after its single answer.
quality_checks: All three characters must contribute to the actor debate.
At least one Cillian phone attempt must be stopped by Patrick.
The actor question must return at least once after being dropped.
Family topics unrelated to the programme should occupy at least 30% of turns.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
